summary: Sets out the charter and rules for the general IETF discussion mailing list, including what topics belong there and what behavior is not acceptable, such as advertising. It is a Best Current Practice. It was replaced by RFC 9245.

plainLanguage.summary: Every big chat room needs rules about what you can talk about and what is not allowed. This sets the rules for the main chat room of the group that makes Internet rules.

subtitle: The rules for what belongs on the general IETF discussion mailing list.

tldr.problem: The IETF's most general mailing list needs clear rules on what is on topic and what is not.
tldr.mechanism: The charter lists the list's two purposes, appropriate and inappropriate postings, and lets the IETF Chair, the IETF Executive Director or a sergeant-at-arms restrict posters who show a pattern of abuse.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3005 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 45). It was updated by RFC 8717 and replaced by RFC 9245.

today: RFC 3005 is obsoleted by RFC 9245 and was updated by RFC 8717. Use the newer charter.

sections.title: Purpose of the List
sections.content:
The IETF discussion list, ietf@ietf.org, serves two purposes. It furthers the development and specification of Internet technology through discussion of technical issues, and it hosts discussions of IETF direction, policy, meetings and procedures.

Because it is the most general IETF mailing list, considerable latitude is allowed. The list is meant for initial discussion only: topics that fall within a working group or well-established list should move there once that is pointed out, unless the working group needs wider input or direction.
sections.plainLanguage: This is the big open room where people start talking about Internet rules. If a topic has its own smaller room, the talk moves there.

sections.title: Appropriate and Inappropriate Posts
sections.content:
Appropriate postings include Last Call discussions of proposed protocol actions, technical issues that are candidates for IETF work but have no e-mail venue yet, IETF administrative policies, questions about IETF meetings, and announcements of events sponsored or endorsed by the Internet Society or IETF.

Inappropriate postings include unsolicited bulk e-mail, subjects unrelated to IETF policy, meetings, activities or technical concerns, unprofessional commentary regardless of subject, and announcements of events that are not sponsored or endorsed by the Internet Society or IETF. Advertising, including job promotion, and discussions of a personal nature are outside the range of acceptable topics.
sections.plainLanguage: Questions and news about the group are welcome. Junk mail, rude remarks and ads are not.

sections.title: Enforcement
sections.content:
The IETF Chair, the IETF Executive Director or a sergeant-at-arms appointed by the Chair is empowered to restrict posting by a person, or of a thread, when the content is inappropriate and represents a pattern of abuse.

They are encouraged to consider the overall nature of an individual's postings and whether a given post is an aberration or typical. Complaints about their decisions should be referred to the IAB.
sections.plainLanguage: A few trusted people can ask someone to stop if they keep breaking the rules. They should look at the whole picture, and anyone who disagrees can complain to a higher group.
